newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 3.

text.p: Sanyo Electric Co Ltd and other leading electrical companies plan to start a discount domestic long-distance phone service for corporate customers from next January. Sanyo plans to offer long-distance phone rates 30 percent lower than those of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp for Tokyo-Osaka calls. Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp are also to start such services next year.

Leading liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) suppliers, including Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd and Nippon Petroleum Gas Co Ltd, plan to raise wholesale prices for propane and butane gas by 30 percent this month. This is due to Saudi Arabia's increase on its export price of LPG to Japan to the highest level in 16 years.
Tonen Corp is expected to see its pre-tax profit fall by seven percent to 14 billion yen in the business year ending December 31 from last year, hit by a slow recovery in gasoline prices.
Nine leading construction companies are expected to see their current profits fall in the business year to March 1997, hit by lower construction orders.

Dai Nippon Printing Co Ltd and Toppan Printing Co Ltd are expected to post higher pre-tax profit in the business year to March 1997. Dai Nippon expects to see its profit rise one percent to 87 billion yen, while Toppan should see a rise of nine percent to 66 billion yen, helped by strong electronics sales and production streamlining.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd plans to double its production capacity of liquid crystal displays (LCDs). It plans to spend 20 billion yen on the project in the year starting next April.

Marubeni Corp has set up a joint venture to develop an iron ore mine in India, in cooperation with an Indian mining company. They hope to produce 150 tonnes of iron ore annually and sell it to iron and steel makers in Japan, Asia and the Middle East.
